proposals.objective: Add residual-stall, oscillatory-divergence, and Courant-excursion rules to the monitor, covering the calm failure modes the spike rule cannot see
proposals.rationale: The lab's own evidence documents a failure the current monitor misses by design: the Re 200 cylinder stalls at residual near 1e-3 with a small force oscillation and exits on the iteration cap looking calm, because a steady solver applied past its regime degrades measurably but never spikes. Detection rules from the monitor standard: a stall is a rolling-median residual improving by less than a factor of 2 over 200 iterations while still above the residualControl target; oscillatory divergence is alternating-sign residual changes with a growing envelope over 50 iterations; a Courant excursion is the reported maximum exceeding the case limit or growing monotonically over 20 steps. A stalled result is UNCONVERGED no matter how smooth its tail, and the prescribed action is the regime check before any rerun buys more iterations. The Courant rule is written now so the first transient run arrives born monitored.
citations: Certonomous Numericist Knowledge Base, Validated Facts 3 And 4
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: The monitor recognizes the graceful-degradation family of failures, so a run that exits on its iteration cap can never be mistaken for evidence again
proposals.decision_note: Owner GO, all proposals, morning 2026-07-25
proposals.dismiss_reason: Implemented and in force, and closed out against a real failure rather than the archive alone. S6 residual stall, S7 oscillatory divergence and S8 Courant excursion were already running; this closes the item by adding S10, the family that catches the Ahmed body primal whose drag was published and withdrawn this week. That run reads converged to every earlier rule: its omega field was pegged at the top of its clipping range while the number the log calls its residual finished at 5.9e-31, because a normalised residual is a ratio and the denominator blew up with the field. S10 names it three independent ways, a ceiling clip, a residual sitting at 1e-20 for a hundred iterations after having been alive while its peers still work, and an unnormalised residual norm ten orders past momentum. All three were swept over the 383 archived solver logs before adoption and together they name exactly one, that run. The healthy coarse solve of the same case raises nothing. One rule measured badly and is recorded, not hidden: S7 ungated fires on 68 of the lab 106 archived steady logs and calls 65 of them fatal, every one a completed run whose results are on the record. Four tightenings were measured and none rescued it. S7 now requires the residual target its own proposal wording implies and stays silent on any field that reached it, and it is filed to the owner as the weakest rule in the standard with withdrawal as the live alternative.

proposals.rationale: The guard rejects a fit whose Richardson value lands more than 15 percent of the measured range width outside that range. proposals.objective: Test whether B3's adjoint failure (PETSc DIVERGED_NANORINF at iteration 0) is caused by a non-finite value already present in the converged primal state, by scanning every primal field cell-by-cell for non-finite entries before the adjoint is launched
proposals.rationale: B3's discrete adjoint dies with DIVERGED_NANORINF at GMRES iteration 0, reproduced identically across four configurations: two primal convergence levels, two objective types, and two ILU fill levels. Mesh quality was checked and cleared. Failing at iteration zero, before any GMRES progress, means the non-finite value is present in the operator or the right-hand side at the moment they are assembled, not generated by the solve. The adjoint linearizes about the converged primal state, so a single cell holding an inf or NaN in any primal field would produce exactly this signature. A converged residual norm does not exclude it: the norm is a sum over cells, and a non-finite entry in a field the residual does not weight can sit there unnoticed. That the failure is invariant to convergence level, objective and preconditioner is the strongest evidence for it - all three are downstream of the state, and none of them would change a poisoned input.
citations: Certonomous DAFoam Case Status, Ladder B3 stage 3 blocker
proposals.cost_basis: estimate, field scan is IO-bound, no solve required to test the hypothesis
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: A cheap test of the only hypothesis that explains all four reproductions at once. If it holds, B3 unblocks and the lab gains a preflight check that belongs in front of every adjoint we ever run. If it fails, we have eliminated the state and the search moves to the operator assembly, which is where it should go next anyway.
proposals.dismiss_reason: Hypothesis tested and KILLED, at zero solver compute. A cell-by-cell scan of every field the adjoint reads - 886,833 numeric tokens across 13 files, including U and UData which the earlier partial check never covered - found zero non-finite values, and the mesh log confirms no degenerate cell volumes. The primal state is finite everywhere, so it is not the poison. Two further candidates were eliminated by structural reasoning rather than compute: the design-variable Jacobian enters only after the adjoint vector is solved, so it cannot sit inside an operator that diverges at iteration zero, and the objective derivative is only the right-hand side, whose norm printed finite for both objectives tested. Search now narrowed to a derivative singularity inside the transpose Jacobian or its preconditioner, most plausibly the low-Reynolds near-wall closure terms at the near-zero turbulence wall boundary condition. Successor test in flight.

proposals.objective: Add a Sobol sensitivity mission type that apportions output variance across the input spreads before any uncertainty reduction campaign is priced
proposals.rationale: The lab propagates input spreads through Monte Carlo but never says which input owns the variance, so reduction work is untargeted. proposals.objective: Test whether A1's sign-flipped leading-edge shape derivative (idx6) is caused by discrete non-differentiability at the wall-function switching threshold, by measuring whether leading-edge cells cross that threshold under the finite-difference perturbation
proposals.rationale: A1's CD/shape check fails on one component: idx6, the leading-edge combo mode, is sign-flipped and accounts for 82.7 percent of the squared-error norm. It is step-independent, survives a 3.65x mesh refinement, and the frozen-wall-distance mechanism was measured to contribute exactly zero. Root cause is unidentified and this is the deepest open question in the ladder. A mechanism nobody has tested: the Spalart-Allmaras wall-function branch is a discrete switch on the near-wall cell state. If leading-edge cells cross that switch between the plus and minus finite-difference perturbations, the function being differenced is not continuous there, so the finite difference is estimating the slope across a step rather than a derivative, and the adjoint, which linearizes one branch only, is right while the check is wrong. That would explain step-independence, which a truncation-error story cannot, and it would explain why only the leading edge misbehaves while mid-chord and aft components agree to 1.5-6.4 percent. The measurement is cheap: instrument the near-wall cell state at each perturbed configuration and count threshold crossings. If none cross, the hypothesis dies and we have eliminated it for good.

Wall-face values were then measured for five fresh independent runs - baseline, the suspect mode plus and minus, and a healthy control mode plus and minus. proposals.objective: Establish how often a solver's convergence reporting can mask a run that did not converge, by classifying every run this lab holds with an automated checker and separately auditing what a sample of published papers on our own validation cases actually state about convergence
proposals.rationale: In a single night this lab found SIX published numbers of its own resting on runs that never met their convergence criterion, including one inside the correction that fixed the first two. They hid in four distinct ways: a normalised residual collapsing to a tiny fixed value while raw statistics showed a blow up; a solver exiting zero having printed a success message over a residual that underflowed to denormal range; a run reaching its iteration cap with no convergence statement while a plausible residual was quoted anyway; and a final residual quoted where the gate tests the initial one. A seventh form was found in the case configuration rather than the log, where the convergence gate named fields the turbulence model does not transport and therefore could never fire. Every instance was found by somebody looking at something else. Two observations make this worth studying rather than merely fixing. First, an automated sweep of 92 run logs classified 55 as not converged, and although the large majority were already known and disclosed, nobody had ever counted. Second, the literature review found that the best known reproduction of one of our validation cases never states a convergence tolerance anywhere in the paper, and that its closest agreement with experiment is attributed by its own authors to a coarse mesh numerical viscosity accident rather than to a modelling result. If a defect this easy to hide occurs six times in one lab's own work in one night, the reasonable prior is that it is widespread, and nobody appears to have measured how widespread.

proposals.objective: Establish whether the cylinder ladder's Strouhal gates are sensitive to near-wall spacing at every rung or only at the highest one, by running a matched-spacing twin at the ladder's best-gated low-Reynolds rung and comparing the shift against the one already measured at the top
proposals.rationale: A matched pair at the ladder's top rung, differing only in first-cell height by 55 percent, moved drag by 7.1 percent, base suction by 6.9 percent and fluctuation amplitude by 3.3 percent , all small against the 50 to 100 percent deviations those quantities carry versus the three-dimensional reference. Strouhal moved 35.1 percent, from 0.2409 to 0.1564, and that is large enough to flip which side of the reference band the run lands on, over-predicting in one member and under-predicting in the other. An independent windowed transform confirmed two genuinely distinct frequency bands rather than a period-detector artifact. So at that rung the Strouhal gate is not a solid measurement. Nothing is known about the lower rungs, which have no twins, and the ladder reports a Strouhal trend ACROSS rungs, and that is a trend whose sensitivity is therefore unquantified at every point but one. The best-supported reading is that the sensitivity belongs to a chaotic-dynamics regime in which a finite window no longer contains one robust dominant frequency, which is consistent with published evidence that two-dimensional confined cylinder wakes are fully chaotic well below this Reynolds number. That reading predicts the low rung will be ROBUST. Falsifiable either way: if the low rung's Strouhal moves comparably under the same spacing change, the sensitivity is not regime-related and every Strouhal gate on this ladder is soft; if it holds within a few percent, the sensitivity has an onset and the lower gates stand.

proposals.objective: Identify the cause of the U-bend case's gradient failure, now known not to share the mesh-warp defect found on the airfoil, by isolating each remaining link of its derivative chain against a finite difference of that link
proposals.rationale: The airfoil's shape-derivative defect was resolved today and traced to the mesh warp's own linearisation. The U-bend was then tested against the same mechanism and CLEARED: its design variables are all single-point, and its two sign-flipped components agree with a finite difference of the warp to 0.32 to 1.30 percent. Yet its real verification still fails badly, at 46.6 percent aggregate with only 5 of 27 components in band, and it carries the same immunities that misled the airfoil investigation for months: a step-size sweep excludes truncation error, and tightening the primal made it worse rather than better, taking two sign flips to three. So this is a second, independent defect and nothing is known about it. The link-by-link isolation strategy is what finally worked on the airfoil after six wrong mechanisms, and it should be applied here rather than guessing again. Three features distinguish this case and are the natural first suspects: an internal duct flow rather than external aerodynamics, an objective that is a pressure difference between two patches rather than an integrated force, and a half model with a symmetry plane. A two-patch difference objective and a symmetry plane are both constructions that can carry a sign error.

proposals.objective: Determine why one case family's adjoint fails to converge at every mesh size tested while another family converges on a larger mesh, and whether the failing family can be fixed by conditioning rather than by hardware or coarsening
proposals.rationale: This proposal was written a few hours ago around a cell-count threshold and that framing is now dead; the measurement that killed it is the reason the question is worth more, not less. Within one transonic, shock-containing, compressible case family the adjoint returns the same linear-solver breakdown at 21,840 cells, at 79,560 cells and at 99,840 cells -- a 4.6-fold range with no exceptions. Within a separate incompressible family it converges cleanly at 63,920 cells, a LARGER mesh than the smallest failing one. So the failure does not track mesh size at all, and three consequences follow. Coarsening as an escape route is definitively dead rather than merely unpromising, which retires a strategy this lab has spent real time on. Buying hardware cannot help, since the smallest failing case peaked at 5.9 GB with the host holding over 20 GB free. And the discriminator is a property of the case, with the obvious candidate being what distinguishes the two families: six transported fields including temperature, transonic, shock-containing, against four or five, incompressible, smooth. An adjoint that is ill-conditioned because the primal carries a shock would be ill-conditioned at any resolution, which is exactly the pattern observed. Testing it means attacking the conditioning directly -- scaling, equilibration, a restarted or flexible Krylov variant -- at a mesh small enough to iterate on quickly, which the 21,840-cell case now provides at seven minutes per attempt. Falsified if the breakdown survives every conditioning treatment at the small mesh, in which case the limitation is structural to this solver's discrete adjoint for shock-containing flows, and that is a finding worth publishing rather than working around.

Saad, Iterative Methods for Sparse Linear Systems, on breakdown and equilibration

proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: Decides whether an entire class of cases -- transonic and shock-containing, which is most of external aerodynamics worth optimising -- is reachable by this adjoint at all. It also hands us a cheap test bed: a seven-minute case that reproduces the failure exactly, where previously the cheapest reproduction took sixteen minutes and was assumed to need a large mesh.

A cheap reproducer exists at 21,840 cells and seven minutes per attempt, so conditioning experiments that were previously assumed to need a large mesh can now be iterated quickly.
proposals.outcome: Answered. The failure is a linear-solver breakdown, not a memory ceiling. The ONERA M6 adjoint returns the same breakdown at 21,840, 42,120, 79,560 and 99,840 cells, so mesh size is not the constraint and coarsening was never going to help. The NASA hump reproduces it independently: DIVERGED_NANORINF at GMRES iteration 0 with Jacobian colouring completing normally and available memory bottoming at 18.99 GB of 30. Two levers remove the NaN and neither converges, and the matrix reordering is implicated in producing it since the failing scripts use rcm where the one working tutorial uses natural. The family that does converge, field inversion, differs in that its warping component is never constructed at all.

proposals.objective: Give the model channel a measured parametric basis: propagate published k-omega SST closure-coefficient intervals through solves on the motorcycle held mesh and report the resulting drag envelope as coefficient-interval evidence alongside the current transferred estimate
proposals.rationale: The model channel today rests on closure-family spread and validation-history transfer; neither measures how much of the answer rides on the closure coefficients themselves. The Schaefer papers supply defensible epistemic intervals with named provenance for every SST coefficient (beta-star in [0.0784, 0.1024] from Wilcox's measured stress ratio, a1 in [0.31, 0.40] which may only be increased, kappa in [0.38, 0.42] from pipe-flow experiments) and show SST is the most coefficient-sensitive of the common RANS models, with beta-star dominating drag and skin friction and a1 rising wherever the flow separates - directly relevant to a bluff body carrying a rider. The recipe holds the 353,578-cell motorcycle mesh and numerics fixed, restarts each case from the converged baseline (the papers' own cost trick), and solves one-at-a-time corner cases for the five coefficients the papers found significant: beta-star, a1, sigma-w1, beta-star/beta1, beta-star/beta2, each at its interval bounds with a1 varied upward only. Ten solves at about six minutes each from measured motorcycle solve times gives roughly 60 core-minutes; the drag envelope across the set is a measured coefficient-interval band, reported as an interval (no probability density assumed), never folded into the quadrature u_val as a sigma. If the band is material against the numerical channel of plus or minus 0.00053 on Cd, a second stage promotes the top three coefficients to a 20-sample Latin Hypercube set (order-2 response surface at oversampling 2, per the papers' design) and runs the new Sobol analysis layer for variance shares, about 120 further core-minutes. Caveat carried honestly: the intervals' provenance is flow-independent but the papers' sensitivity rankings are transonic; our solves measure the incompressible separated-flow ranking locally, which is the point.

proposals.objective: Rebuild Ling's tensor-basis neural network and run his own Reynolds-number-generalisation experiment on the closure challenge's duct family: train on AR_1, AR_3, AR_5 and AR_10 at Ret 180, hold AR_7_Ret_180 for hyper-parameters, and predict the three scored duct cases without opening them
proposals.rationale: Ling, Kurzawski and Templeton trained on a duct at Re_b 3500 and tested on a duct at Re_b 2000, a Reynolds-number generalisation inside one geometry family. The benchmark's duct split is that same experiment: AR_1_Ret_360 holds the aspect ratio fixed and moves the Reynolds number, and AR_14_Ret_180 does the reverse and extrapolates beyond the trained aspect-ratio range of 1 to 10. The duct is where this lab's deficit to the rank two entry is largest, and it is the one family where the full ten-tensor basis is live, since the secondary flow is three-dimensional. The Sandia reference implementation is public under BSD-3-Clause. This proposal reproduces the architecture and the experiment design; it explicitly does NOT reproduce the paper's Table I, because two of the six training flows behind those numbers are Sandia and Stanford internal simulations with no public archive named in the paper, so the training database cannot be assembled from the paper. That non-reproducibility is itself the recorded finding of the reading.
proposals.cost_basis: measured, from this lab's own hardware, plus one stated extrapolation. Ladder-B rung B2 timed the benchmark duct primals serially on this box: AR_1_Ret_360 at 8 s (0.13 core-min) and AR_3_Ret_360 at 76 s (1.27 core-min), both runs completed and agreeing with the benchmark's shipped baseline field. AR_14_Ret_180 was not timed; scaling AR_3_Ret_360 linearly by cell count (8,748 to 31,819) gives roughly 5 core-min and is labelled an extrapolation, not a measurement. Propagation on all three scored cases is therefore about 7 core-min per model. The balance is feature and label extraction over the 57,434 training and validation cells and pointwise training of an 8-layer, 30-node network on CPU. The paper reports NO compute cost of any kind, so no part of this estimate is taken from it. Ling's Spearmint Bayesian hyper-parameter search is deliberately out of scope and unbudgeted: its cost is undisclosed and this proposal uses the paper's own stated values instead, 8 hidden layers, 30 nodes, learning rate 2.5e-7.
proposals.gate: Out of sample by construction and checked, not asserted: sdk/scripts/closure_in_sample_gate.py must return PASS with the training declaration present, and the three scored duct cases AR_1_Ret_360, AR_3_Ret_360 and AR_14_Ret_180 must never be opened for training or validation. Second gate, a priori before a posteriori: the TBNN must beat the k-omega SST baseline on RMSE of the anisotropy tensor b against the held-out AR_7_Ret_180 LES field before any solver modification is attempted. Third, the DNS-b control of the paper's section IV.B must be run alongside any propagation, so that closure error is separated from k and omega transport error rather than conflated with it.
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: The second rung of the M2 reproduction ladder, standing up on data already in the tree. It also answers a question the taxonomy in docs/research/CLOSURE_METHODS.md left open by ranking TBNN on code availability alone: whether an invariant tensor-basis network trained only on low-Reynolds ducts transfers to the scored ducts at all. A negative result is worth as much as a positive one and costs the same hour.

proposals.objective: Reproduce step one of SpaRTA on the curved backward-facing step: extract the two additive model-form corrections b_ij^Delta and R from the shipped LES fields by k-corrective-frozen-RANS, add them back as static fields to a k-omega SST solver, and hit the paper's published Table 1 row for CBFS13700
proposals.rationale: Three facts found by reading the paper in full make this the cheapest genuine rung on the M2 ladder. First, k-corrective-frozen-RANS needs no adjoint and no optimiser: it solves the omega transport equation passively with Ui, k and bij frozen at their high-fidelity values and takes the k-equation residual as R, converging in the authors' words after a few hundred iterations. Every blocker on this lab's field-inversion line, the warpDeriv defect and the gradient conditioning, is therefore irrelevant to it. Second, the benchmark ships SpaRTA's own case: the paper states the CBFS mesh is 140 by 150 cells and the clone's polyMesh header reads nCells 21000, which is that product exactly, and each case directory carries 0/U_LES, 0/k_LES and 0/tauij_LES, precisely the three full fields the method consumes, on the same mesh, with no interpolation. Third, there is a published number to hit, so this is a reproduction and not an exercise. Scoped to step one deliberately: the paper's own cross-validation is 75 CFD simulations for CBFS alone, which at this lab's measured rate is about 37 core-hours, and none of it is worth committing until the extraction is shown to work. Ladder-B rung B2 recorded that Ofpp cannot resolve the #include macros in those LES field files and silently returns None; that blocker is specific to the Python reader and does not bite here, because k-corrective-frozen-RANS runs inside OpenFOAM, whose own dictionary parser expands #include natively.
proposals.cost_basis: measured, on this hardware, on this exact case and mesh. Ladder-B rung B2 ran the benchmark's CBFS case, 21,000 cells, k-omega SST, serial, to its designed 30,000 iterations in 1,753.3 s CPU and 1,770 s wall, 29.5 core-minutes, and the converged field agreed with the benchmark's own shipped baseline to 0.068 percent scaled MAE. That run completed, is not superseded and is not the run this proposal would replace. The frozen extraction solves one transport equation for a few hundred iterations and is bounded well under 2 core-minutes against that per-iteration rate; the validation propagation restarts from the baseline solution and is bounded at one full primal, 29.5 core-minutes. Sixty core-minutes carries a full retry. Memory from the same rung: MemAvailable was 20.4 GB before and 13.0 GB after three serial runs including this one, never near the 6 GB threshold. The paper's own compute disclosure was NOT used for any of this: it prices only the model selection step, at the order of a minute on a consumer laptop for 15,000 data points, and leaves all 184 of its cross-validation simulations unpriced.
proposals.gate: Primary, quantitative, published: with b_ij^Delta and R added as static fields, the mean-squared error of the reconstructed velocity normalised by the baseline k-omega SST must land within a factor of two of the paper's Table 1 CBFS13700 value of 0.22703, and must be below 1.0 as a hard floor since a value above 1.0 means the extraction made the field worse than the model it corrects. The Reynolds-stress ratio is reported alongside against the paper's 0.4949 but is not gated, because Table 1 shows the method's own stress reconstruction is the weaker of the two on every case. Secondary and non-negotiable: sdk/scripts/closure_in_sample_gate.py must return PASS with the CBFS training declaration present. CBFS13700 is a benchmark training case, not one of the eight scored cases, so no test truth is opened at any point.
proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: The third rung of the M2 ladder, and the first closure correction this lab would extract from real high-fidelity data rather than from a synthetic tutorial. It also settles the open question the reading raised: whether the honest cost of SpaRTA is the one-minute regression the paper advertises or the thirty-seven core-hours of CFD cross-validation it does not price. Failing the gate is informative too, because the extraction step has no free parameters worth blaming.

proposals.objective: Test whether the ONERA M6 primal residual plateau at 1.02e-06 is caused by wall resolution sitting in the buffer layer, by re-running the case on a wall-resolved mesh (yPlus below 1) and on a clean wall-function mesh (yPlus above 30) and observing whether the plateau moves
proposals.rationale: The M6 act ships as a documented failure: the primal ran its full 3,000 iterations and missed its own 1e-08 gate at 1.02e-06. The turbulence equation alone is responsible - momentum, energy and pressure all satisfy the gate at 1e-07 to 1e-08. The residual reached 1e-06 inside the first quarter of the run and changed by a factor of 0.997 across the entire final third, so it is a fixed point rather than slow convergence and more iterations cannot help. The mesh has yPlus spanning 5.21 to 103.5 with mean 33.8, which straddles the buffer layer: too coarse to resolve the viscous sublayer, too fine for a clean wall function. A turbulence equation that cannot settle while every other equation does is consistent with the near-wall treatment being ambiguous across the surface. This is a hypothesis, not a conclusion, and the run that produced it does not test it. Two meshes settle it: if the plateau clears on either, wall treatment is the cause; if it survives both, the cause is elsewhere and we have narrowed it sharply.

proposals.objective: Locate the Reynolds number at which a two-dimensional cylinder wake stops producing a time-mean recirculation bubble, by running the single intermediate rung that halves the interval in which the transition is now known to lie
proposals.rationale: Measured tonight across three rungs, all extracted by identical code against a definition confirmed word-for-word in the reference literature: mean recirculation length 0.397 diameters, then 0.254, then none at all. The third is a departure from the trend, not a continuation -- extrapolating the first two predicts about 0.165, and the method resolved 0.254 cleanly one rung earlier, so it would have seen 0.165. The mechanism is measured rather than assumed: reversal FREQUENCY is flat across all three rungs at 34 to 48 percent, while the amplitude of forward-going excursions grows from 0.22 to 0.52 to 0.81, so the bubble is swamped in the average rather than extinguished in the flow. Meanwhile the three-dimensional bubble GROWS with Reynolds number over the same interval, so the two dimensionalities diverge rather than one merely lagging. The transition therefore sits inside a factor-of-two window and one intermediate rung halves it. A falsifiable prediction is already recorded: the intermediate rung either shows a detectable bubble near 0.16 to 0.20, supporting smooth extinction reaching zero close to the upper rung, or shows none, placing the onset lower. Either outcome is decisive, which is the property a rung should have before it is worth its compute.

Parnaudeau et al. (2008), recirculation length defined as the sign change of centreline mean streamwise velocity

proposals.expected_knowledge_gain: A located transition rather than an interval, on the ladder's sharpest result. Every other quantity here says two dimensions is high by some percentage; this one says the mean wake differs in kind, which is far better evidence for a dimensionality attribution than any deviation figure.

proposals.objective: Determine whether a gradient computed on a coarse adjoint mesh is accurate enough to drive optimization on a fine primal mesh, by measuring gradient direction agreement (cosine similarity, not just magnitude) between coarse and fine adjoints on the one case where both are affordable
proposals.rationale: The adjoint memory wall blocks four cases and the reflex response is to buy a bigger machine. That may be the wrong purchase. Optimization does not need an accurate gradient magnitude; it needs an accurate gradient DIRECTION, because the line search recovers the step length. If the coarse-mesh adjoint points the same way as the fine-mesh adjoint, the wall stops being a blocker and becomes a cost-management technique, and it does so on hardware we already own. A4 already exercises this pattern informally, using a 2,777-cell adjoint mesh against a 45,760-cell primal, but nobody has measured whether the resulting direction is right - only that its magnitude lands within 10.04 percent on a single scalar design variable, which says nothing about direction in a many-variable space. The measurement wanted is cosine similarity across the full design-variable vector at several coarsening ratios, on a case small enough that the fine-mesh adjoint is affordable as ground truth.

proposals.objective: Determine how tight the model-form uncertainty band on hump reattachment can be made while still containing the experiment, by replacing the extremal anisotropy limiting states with physically weighted perturbations and measuring the containment/width trade-off curve
proposals.rationale: The D9 result is the lab's flagship epistemic claim: the band contains the known +13.95 percent reattachment error, and the prediction that it would was written before the runs. But the band spans 0.5278 to 1.2534, a factor of 2.4, and the record says plainly that containment is necessary and not sufficient. The band's width comes from channel 3 taking the barycentric map's extremal limiting states, which are bounds by construction and are not predictions. The open question, stated in the record itself, is not whether the band contains but how tight it can be made while still containing. That is a research question with a curve as its answer, not a single number: sweep the perturbation magnitude from extremal down toward zero and find where containment breaks. The point at which it breaks is itself the interesting result, because it measures how much of the band is doing real work. Channel 2, documented model bias from the literature, was never incorporated and belongs in this study.

proposals.objective: Test whether the anisotropy-perturbation uncertainty method destroys the very quantity it is built to bound, by establishing at what perturbation magnitude the separation bubble stops being a single closing structure and whether a converged solution exists beyond that point at all
proposals.rationale: Today's sweep produced a result more interesting than the curve it was meant to produce. Only two perturbation magnitudes met their convergence gate, and the larger of the two moved the reattachment point AWAY from the experiment rather than toward it. Every magnitude that moves toward the experimental value failed to converge, with severity rising in step, and the flow fragments into multiple separation and reattachment events from a magnitude of 0.10 onward. So the scalar the band is built on stops being well defined in exactly the range where the band would have to be tightened. If non-convergence and fragmentation are the same phenomenon, then tightening is not merely circular, it is unreachable, and that is a genuine intrinsic limit of the method rather than a failure of this attempt. Separation position stayed single-valued and smooth throughout, which extends the known separation-is-easy-reattachment-is-hard asymmetry from accuracy into numerical well-posedness. Distinguishing an intrinsic limit from a mesh-and-scheme artefact is the crux, because only the second is fixable.

proposals.objective: Derive the NACA 0012 finite-wing reference, then re-run its ladder with the boundary layer resolved
proposals.rationale: Two independent defects sit under this credential's 148 percent deviation, and both were measured on 2026-07-31. First the reference: its drag coefficient of 0.009 was hand-set in the lab's first commit and has never been touched, its tolerance of 0.30 is hand-picked prose, and its confidence reads medium. That is the same shape as the NACA 4412 reference of 0.030 which the lab already replaced with a derivation and an RSS band. Second the solve: all three ladder rungs were meshed with layer addition switched off at chord Reynolds 1.000e6, so there are no boundary-layer cells at all, the identical defect that superseded the 4412 credential. The ladder reads 27,265 cells at 0.028688, 67,356 at 0.022290 and 140,580 at 0.012053, monotone decreasing and not grid-conclusive, and the credential grades the middle rung while the study's own working value is already the finest. On the finest rung the deviation is 34 percent, not 148. The recorded root cause, a three-dimensional wing graded against two-dimensional section data, is refuted by the wing's own solved lift: at a lift coefficient of -0.000795 on a measured aspect ratio of 3.000 the induced drag is 8.7e-08, six orders of magnitude below the section drag, so there is no induced-drag penalty here to explain the gap. Deriving at near-zero lift also removes the flaw that makes the 4412 derivation self-referential, since a reference that collapses to the section term cannot be moved by the lift error it is meant to detect. An independent anchor is already indexed for the cross-check: the NASA Turbulence Modeling Resource NACA 0012 validation, CFL3D with SST on the 897x257 grid at zero incidence, drag coefficient 0.0080937, though at Reynolds 6e6 and Mach 0.15 rather than this case's Reynolds 1e6, and computed rather than measured, so the Reynolds gap travels with it.

proposals.objective: Determine whether the non-asymptotic verdicts on the Ahmed body and B-52 refinement ladders come from an insufficient refinement ratio or from genuinely non-monotone grid convergence, by re-running each with a constant ratio and reporting the observed order of accuracy
proposals.rationale: Two headline geometries report ladders not in the asymptotic range, and both consequently carry conservative bands rather than extrapolated ones - the B-52 at plus or minus 0.0063 on a Cd of 0.0472, which is 13 percent, and the Ahmed body held back from the validated tier specifically because its ladder was inconclusive. The existing ladders use unequal and in places small cell-count ratios, and the B-52's rungs are non-monotone: 0.0551, 0.0448, 0.0491, 0.0472, 0.0496, 0.0523 as cells rise. Standard practice requires a constant refinement ratio to compute an observed order p at all, and without p there is no Richardson extrapolation and no grid-convergence index. The current verdicts may therefore be reporting a defect in the experiment design rather than in the solutions.
